q: The maximum height of a threshold is ___ mm.
n: The item gives 50 mm as the maximum height of an ordinary door threshold. On accessible routes BP 344 is far stricter, at 12 mm maximum. Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), doors and thresholds.

q: The preferred viewing distance from the eye to the front surface of a computer screen is ____mm.
n: A computer screen is best viewed about 500–900 mm from the eye, roughly arm's length. Source: ANSI/HFES 100 (Human Factors Engineering of Computer Workstations).

q: The height of grab bars from the floor is ___ mm.
n: Grab bars are mounted at about 800 mm from the floor (the 2024 BP 344 IRR puts them 300 mm above a 450 mm seat, about 750 mm). Source: BP 344 IRR (2024 amendment), toilets.

q: Which is NOT an anthropometric measurement?
n: Anthropometric measurements are body dimensions: height, weight, circumferences. Health is not one. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension & Interior Space.

q: What is the average height of a Filipino in centimeters?
n: Filipino men average about 162–163 cm in height. Source: NCD Risk Factor Collaboration (NCD-RisC) height data; FNRI National Nutrition Survey.

q: What is the average height of a Filipina in centimeters?
n: Filipino women average about 150–152 cm in height. Source: NCD-RisC height data; FNRI National Nutrition Survey.

q: What is the opening inlet height for windows?
n: For cross ventilation, inlets are placed low, about 0.90 m, so incoming air sweeps through the occupied zone. Source: Givoni, Climate Considerations in Building and Urban Design; Olgyay, Design with Climate.

q: What is the opening outlet height for windows?
n: Outlets are placed high, about 2.10 m, to exhaust warm air rising to the ceiling (stack effect). Source: Givoni, Climate Considerations in Building and Urban Design.

q: What is the standard shower wall height?
n: Shower walls are commonly tiled to about 2,100 mm, door-head height, to protect against splashing. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Interior Design; tile industry practice (TCNA).

q: Identify the height of a regular counter.
n: The item gives 90–120 cm for regular counters. Kitchen work counters are about 90 cm and service counters up to about 110–120 cm. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension & Interior Space; Time-Saver Standards for Interior Design.

q: Identify the height of a tall bar counter.
n: Tall bar counters are about 105–110 cm, paired with stools about 75–80 cm high. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension & Interior Space.

q: Identify the height of an extra tall bar counter.
n: Extra-tall bar counters run about 115–120 cm. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension & Interior Space.

q: Identify the height of a stool for a regular counter.
n: Stools for a regular-height bar counter are about 75–80 cm high, about 30 cm below the counter. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension & Interior Space.

q: Identify the height of a stool for an extra tall counter.
n: Stools for extra-tall counters range up to about 90 cm, given in the item as 90–120 cm, keeping about 25–30 cm between seat and counter top. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension & Interior Space.

q: Which zone, about 46 to 122 cm, is used for talking with family and close friends?
n: Hall's personal distance (about 46–122 cm, 1.5–4 ft) is used for conversation with family and close friends. Source: Hall, The Hidden Dimension (1966).

q: What applied science fits design to people's characteristics for safe, efficient use?
n: Ergonomics (human factors) is the applied science of fitting design to people's characteristics for safe, efficient use. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension & Interior Space; IEA definition.

q: The size or proportion of something relative to an accepted standard of measurement.
n: Mechanical scale is the size or proportion of something relative to an accepted standard of measurement (metres, feet). Source: Ching, Architecture: Form, Space & Order.

q: What is a dimension set by body movement, such as reach or stride?
n: A functional (dynamic) dimension is set by body movement, such as reach or stride. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension & Interior Space.

q: What is the science of signs?
n: Semiotics is the science of signs and symbols and how they convey meaning. Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, semiotics; Broadbent, Signs, Symbols and Architecture.

q: A distance of 12 ft or more is:
n: 12 ft (≈3.7 m) or more is Hall's public distance. Public distance suits lectures and speakers addressing groups. Source: Hall, The Hidden Dimension.

q: A distance of 0–18 in. is:
n: 0–18 in. (0–45 cm) is Hall's intimate distance. Intimate distance is reserved for close relationships, comforting and whispering. Source: Hall, The Hidden Dimension.

q: What is the space within 3 ft used in furniture design?
n: Within about 3 ft lies personal space, the zone that furniture groupings for conversation work within. Source: Hall, The Hidden Dimension; Panero & Zelnik.

q: What is the space within 1 ft used in furniture design?
n: Within about 1 ft lies intimate space. This closest zone is used for physical contact and furniture meant for close companions, such as loveseats. Source: Hall, The Hidden Dimension; Panero & Zelnik.

q: Which proxemic zone suits formal meetings and business talks?
n: Social distance, about 4–12 ft, suits formal meetings and business conversations. Source: Hall, The Hidden Dimension.

q: Minimum depth of an overhead cabinet.
n: Overhead kitchen cabinets are about 300 mm deep, so they clear the head over a 600 mm counter. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data (kitchens); Panero & Zelnik.

q: What is the height on center if you are to mount an artwork?
n: Artwork is commonly hung with its centre about 1,500 mm above the floor, near average eye level. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Interior Design; gallery hanging practice.

q: Maximum height of shower head mounting.
n: Shower heads are commonly mounted up to about 2.00 m above the floor. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Interior Design; Panero & Zelnik.

q: Recommended distance of the edge of the dining table from a wall.
n: Leave about 900 mm from the table edge to a wall so a chair can be pulled out and a person can pass. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension & Interior Space (dining clearances).

q: Recommended size of a three-seater sofa.
n: A typical three-seater sofa is about 700 mm deep × 2.00 m long (the depth varies by model). Source: Neufert, Architects' Data (living room furniture).

q: Height of a dining table.
n: Dining tables are about 750 mm high. This height lets a seated diner (seat about 450 mm) eat comfortably with knee clearance under the table. Source: Neufert, Architects' Data; Panero & Zelnik.

q: Height of working table for Filipina.
n: For an average Filipina, a work table height of about 0.75 m suits seated work. Source: Panero & Zelnik, Human Dimension & Interior Space; Philippine anthropometric data.
